definitions.gloss: reluctantly; unwillingly; having no other choice
definitions.explanation: Describes doing something because there is no alternative, not because one wants to.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}がなかったので、{仕方|しかた}なくタクシーに{乗|の}った。
examples.english: Since there were no trains, I reluctantly took a taxi.

examples.japanese: {仕方|しかた}なく{残業|ざんぎょう}することになった。
examples.english: I had no choice but to work overtime.

examples.japanese: {誰|だれ}も{手伝|てつだ}ってくれないから、{仕方|しかた}なく{一人|ひとり}でやった。
examples.english: Since no one would help me, I had no choice but to do it alone.

notes:
FORMATION:
{仕方|しかた} (way/method) + ない (not exist) + く (adverb form)

From {仕方|しかた}がない meaning 'there's no way/it can't be helped.'

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
・{仕方|しかた}がない / しょうがない - it can't be helped
・{仕方|しかた}なしに - reluctantly (slightly more literary)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{嫌々|いやいや} - reluctantly, unwillingly (emphasizes dislike)
・やむを{得|え}ず - unavoidably (formal)
・{渋々|しぶしぶ} - reluctantly (shows visible reluctance)

NUANCE:
{仕方|しかた}なく implies acceptance of the situation; {嫌々|いやいや} emphasizes reluctance and displeasure.
